title: LangGraph documentation: persistence
snippet: Checkpointers save graph state per thread, so a run can resume after a crash or pause for human approval. MemorySaver is in-process; SqliteSaver and PostgresSaver persist to disk.

title: When a tool loop is enough
snippet: A while-loop over bind_tools covers most single-turn support flows. A graph earns its place when you need branching, parallel retrieval, or state that outlives the process. The extra layer is not free: every node is another place to test.

title: Support agent architecture: classify, retrieve, draft, approve
snippet: A common production pattern is four nodes and one approval gate: classify the ticket, retrieve policy, draft with citations, then require a human before any refund executes. State and audit trails matter more than the model choice.

title: LangGraph in production: what teams report
snippet: Teams cite per-node traces and resumable runs as the main benefits. Smaller teams often keep a plain loop until they need checkpointing or human-in-the-loop, then migrate the loop into a graph without changing the prompts.

title: Comparing agent frameworks in 2026
snippet: Framework choice matters less than eval coverage. LangGraph is common where state must survive a process; lighter runtimes dominate single-process prototypes. Most migrations are driven by an operational requirement, not a benchmark.
